summary: The article provides a generally accurate overview of FCNR deposits and GIFT City for NRIs, with most claims verified against authoritative sources. However, some details regarding interest rate ceilings and tax exemptions for returning NRIs require clarification.

claims.claim: Interest rates on FCNR deposits are determined by individual banks, subject to Reserve Bank of India (RBI) guidelines. Banks are free to determine their own interest rates on FCNR (B) deposits, provided that such rates are not higher than the corresponding LIBOR/SWAP rates for the respective currency and maturity as on the last working day of the preceding month.
claims.note: RBI guidelines state that interest rates should be within the ceiling of LIBOR/SWAP rates for the respective currency/maturity plus a certain basis points (e.g., 200 or 300 basis points depending on tenure), not simply 'not higher than' LIBOR/SWAP rates.

claims.claim: For NRIs, the interest earned on FCNR deposits is exempt from income tax in India.
claims.note: Interest earned on FCNR (B) deposits is exempt from income tax in India for NRIs.

claims.claim: The minimum tenure for an FCNR (B) deposit is typically one year. The maximum tenure can go up to five years, though specific banks might offer different ranges.
claims.note: FCNR (B) deposits can be opened for a minimum tenure of 1 year and a maximum tenure of 5 years.

claims.claim: Deposits in FCNR accounts with scheduled commercial banks are covered by the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) for up to ₹5 lakhs per depositor per bank, similar to other eligible deposits.
claims.note: Each depositor in a bank is insured up to a maximum of ₹5,00,000 for both principal and interest amount held by them in the same right and capacity.

claims.claim: IFSCA provides a single-window clearance system and a progressive regulatory framework designed to facilitate ease of doing business for financial institutions and investors.
claims.note: IFSCA has developed a Single Window IT System (SWITS) to streamline application procedures for setting up units in IFSCs, integrating approvals from various regulators.

claims.claim: For NRIs, investments made through IFSC entities can offer tax efficiencies, depending on the specific product and investor's tax residency. These include: Exemption from various Indian taxes for entities operating within the IFSC, such as Goods and Services Tax (GST) on services rendered within the IFSC, and certain income tax exemptions for a period.
claims.note: GIFT City offers tax benefits such as exemption from GST on services rendered within the IFSC and certain income tax exemptions for entities. For NRIs, investments can offer tax efficiencies, including no TDS on income and reduced capital gains tax on certain investments.

claims.claim: The FCNR carve-out is one of the most valuable tools in returning NRI planning. Our Repatriation of Assets page covers the broader cross-border framework. Is agricultural income earned in India taxable for an NRI?
claims.note: While FCNR interest is tax-exempt for NRIs, the article implies this exemption continues for returning NRIs in RNOR status until maturity. While some sources suggest the FCNR interest exemption survives the RNOR window, it's crucial to note that upon becoming a Resident and Ordinarily Resident (ROR), the tax treatment changes, and the interest may become taxable.
